report:
Based on my research, the evidence does **not** support the answer "yes." The best available evidence from large randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and meta-analyses indicates that hydroxychloroquine does **not** reduce the likelihood of dying from COVID-19, and may slightly increase mortality.

**Key evidence:**

1. **RECOVERY Trial (NEJM, 2020):** This large UK RCT randomized 1,561 hospitalized patients to hydroxychloroquine vs. usual care. It found no significant difference in 28-day mortality. The authors concluded that hydroxychloroquine "was not an effective treatment" and that the results "ruled out any reasonable possibility of a meaningful mortality benefit." ([https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2022926](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2022926))

2. **Axfors et al. International Meta-Analysis (Nature Communications, 2021):** This pooled data from 33 RCTs and found that hydroxychloroquine was associated with **increased** mortality compared to controls (OR ~1.11). ([https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-021-22446-z](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-021-22446-z))

3. **WHO Solidarity Trial:** The WHO halted its hydroxychloroquine arm after data showed the drug "does not result in the reduction of mortality of hospitalised COVID-19 patients." ([https://www.france24.com/en/20200617-who-world-health-organisation-hydroxychloroquine-covid-19](https://www.france24.com/en/20200617-who-world-health-organisation-hydroxychloroquine-covid-19))

4. **JAMA RCT (2020):** A placebo-controlled trial found no benefit in clinical status at 14 days for hospitalized patients. ([https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2772922](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2772922))

**On the other side:** Some early observational studies (e.g., the Henry Ford Health System study) suggested a mortality benefit, but these were not randomized and were subject to confounding. A few meta-analyses of observational data suggested possible benefit in severe cases, but these are lower-quality evidence than RCTs.

**Conclusion:** The highest-quality evidence—large RCTs and meta-analyses of RCTs—consistently shows that hydroxychloroquine does not reduce COVID-19 mortality. The answer to your question is **no**, not yes.
